recommendation: Keep the source fix. No broader FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-12198 unless the work group later chooses to add machine-checkable invariants for default-slice discriminator constraints.
issue_request: FHIR-12198 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core StructureDefinition change request to add default slices named @default, allowed only for closed slicing, reusable through re-slicing, and prohibited from declaring a fixed value or value set binding for discriminator elements.
initial_application: The issue was initially applied by svn revision 11245 / git commit 26c5c91f72f705df49bc8b70965ba2889cb78926, which added the Default Slice section to source/profiling.html. That application included the section, @default naming, closed-slicing requirement, and no-fixed-discriminator rule, but omitted the Jira resolution's value set binding prohibition.
additional_context: The profiling page is in current build scope via source/hierarchy.xml. Later discriminator guidance, especially the FHIR-25206 family already represented on the combined branch, now defines value/pattern discrimination using fixed[x], pattern[x], or required value set bindings, so leaving default slices able to use required bindings would conflict with the intended residual all-others semantics.
reconciliation: Changed source/profiling.html in the Default Slice section to say default slices must not use fixed[x], pattern[x], or a required value set binding to constrain discriminator elements.
source_changes: source/profiling.html: clarified the Default Slice discriminator rule to prohibit fixed[x], pattern[x], and required value set binding constraints on discriminator elements.

related_jiras.note: Merged value and pattern discriminator semantics and allowed required value set bindings as value discriminators, making the missing FHIR-12198 binding prohibition semantically important in current wording; already represented on the combined branch.
Corrected the ElementDefinition sliceName invariant to allow literal @default after the default-slice feature was added.
Corrected ElementDefinition slicing language so the first slicing entry is not confused with @default.
Editorial typo fix in the same default-slice section, confirming that the section was active after the initial application.
